info.name: Conversation Assignment API
info.description:
Postman collection for the Conversation Assignment API (NestJS and MongoDB).

**Before you run it**
1. Start MongoDB and the API (see the README): `docker compose up -d --wait` (MongoDB and Kafka), then `npx nx serve api`.
2. Import this file into Postman.
3. Run the whole collection with the Collection Runner, in order. Later folders use the ids that earlier requests save as collection variables.

**Authentication.** There is no login. Each request sends three headers: `x-user-id`, `x-workspace-id` and `x-role`, taken from the variables below. Requests that need another role or workspace override them.

**Variables.** The defaults below are collection variables. For a different host, user or workspace, import `postman/local.postman_environment.json`, edit its values and select it: an environment value overrides the collection default, so nothing in the collection needs changing.

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `baseUrl` | `http://localhost:3000` | Where the API runs |
| `userId` | `user_123` | The acting user, recorded as `assignedBy` |
| `workspaceId` | `workspace_1` | The caller's workspace |
| `role` | `manager` | `admin`, `manager` or `agent` |
| `adminUserId` | `user_admin` | A second user, used for the admin requests |
| `otherWorkspaceId` | `workspace_2` | A different workspace, for isolation checks |
| `unknownId` | `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` | A well-formed id that does not exist |

The remaining variables (`agentId`, `agent2Id`, `foreignAgentId`, `conversationId`, `closedConversationId`, `nextToken` and the others) are filled in by test scripts while the collection runs. Agent emails are generated per run, so the collection can be run repeatedly against the same database.

**Ids.** Ids are 24-character hex strings. The specification's examples such as `conv_123` are rejected with 400, and some requests send them on purpose.

**Command line.** `npx newman run postman/assignment-api.postman_collection.json` runs every request and its tests.

item.description: Run in order: later requests use the agent and conversation created earlier. `PATCH` and `DELETE` only send a request (`200`, `commandId`, `status: requested`); a consumer applies it, so the test scripts read the conversation until the change shows. The error cases (role, existence, workspace, closed conversation, bad ids) are answered immediately, before anything is sent. An answer of `503` (Kafka unreachable) cannot be shown here; see `npm run demo:kafka-down`.
